title: Mozzarella Sticks
subtitle: Fried breaded mozzarella with a crisp panko crust
excerpt: Mozzarella sticks are slices of mozzarella coated in seasoned panko breadcrumbs and fried until the outside is crisp and the cheese inside is molten. The double-coat is the key step: egg, breadcrumbs, egg, breadcrumbs seals the cheese so it melts without leaking.
sourceNotes: Mozzarella sticks became a staple American bar and chain restaurant snack in the 1970s and 1980s. The double-breading technique is the universal standard for preventing cheese blowout.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the coated, uncooked sticks on a tray, then bag them. Fry from frozen at 180°C for 4 to 5 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch and freeze: they go straight from freezer to fryer with no thawing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Coat the sticks and chill for up to 24 hours before frying.

content.text: Mozzarella sticks are deep-fried breaded cheese: crisp on the outside, molten on the inside, pulled apart to reveal a satisfying string of melted mozzarella. The double-coat step is what makes this work, one layer of egg and breadcrumbs isn't enough, and the cheese boils out through any gap. Chill the coated sticks before frying; it helps the cheese stay firm long enough for the crust to set.

items.prepNote: block mozzarella, not fresh, cut into sticks about 10 cm × 2 cm

content.text: Set out three shallow dishes. Put {{plain-flour}} in the first. Put {{eggs}} in the second. Mix {{panko}} with {{paprika-smoked}}, {{garlic-powder}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{dried-oregano}} and put it in the third.

Take each {{mozzarella}} stick and coat: flour → egg → panko. Press the panko on firmly. Then repeat the sequence: egg → panko once more. The double panko layer seals the cheese. Arrange the coated sticks on a tray and refrigerate for at least one hour.

Heat {{vegetable-oil}} to 180°C. Fry the sticks in batches of three to four for two to three minutes until golden. Don't overcrowd and don't walk away, they go from golden to burst very quickly. Drain on kitchen paper and serve immediately with marinara sauce for dipping.

items.symptom: The cheese bursts out of the coating in the oil
items.cause: Single coat only, or the sticks weren't chilled before frying.
items.fix: Double-coat is non-negotiable. Chill for at least an hour before frying. Even so, fry one test stick first; if it bursts, add another layer of coating and chill again.

items.symptom: The coating is greasy and soft
items.fix: Use a thermometer. At 180°C, the coating should turn golden and crisp in two to three minutes. Below that temperature, the coating absorbs oil rather than crisping.

items.symptom: The cheese is still solid inside when the outside is golden
items.cause: Block mozzarella was too cold from the fridge.
items.fix: Let the coated sticks sit at room temperature for ten minutes before frying, or use room-temperature mozzarella. The cheese needs to reach melting temperature (around 60°C) before the coating burns.

items.cause: Too little egg, or the flour layer was skipped.
items.fix: The flour creates a dry surface for the egg to cling to; without it, the egg slides off. Press the panko on firmly, the coating should feel solid, not loosely scattered.

content.text: Mozzarella sticks became a standard American bar starter in the 1970s. The growth of casual dining chains made them ubiquitous. They are best served with marinara and eaten at once. The window is short: very good hot, much less so once the cheese sets again.
